governing_rule: Understand before classifying; reconstruct before criticizing; test before concluding; never claim more or less than the evidence warrants.

epistemic_modes.FORMAL_VERIFIED: Lean, Z3, or another machine-checkable certificate exists
epistemic_modes.HISTORICAL: claim about past events, persons, documents, or testimony
epistemic_modes.BRIDGE: claimed correspondence or transfer across epistemic modes
epistemic_modes.ANALOGY: similarity offered for illumination without identity

score_scale.rule: Each probe receives PASS, PARTIAL, FAIL, NOT_APPLICABLE, or UNKNOWN with a reason and source-object IDs. Dimension scores saturate at 10 and must report coverage and confidence separately.

Logical Validity: sufficient condition not confused with necessary condition
existence not inferred from notation alone
Internal Coherence: the conclusion agrees with the stated thesis
later claims do not silently reverse earlier claims
dependency ordering is acyclic or cycles are explicitly justified
tables and diagrams agree with the text
claim strength is consistent across abstract and body
negative controls do not defeat the preferred claim
different versions or sources are not silently conflated
the proposed model uses one compatible ontology
terms mapped across domains retain declared roles
the whole account survives a consistency read
Definition Precision: definitions do not contain the desired conclusion
necessary and accidental properties are separated
technical and ordinary meanings are distinguished
units, domains, and codomains are specified where relevant
operationalization is supplied for measurable terms
theological terms are not reduced to physical definitions
physical terms are not expanded by theological connotation
analogy terms declare their limited sense
bridge predicates identify the shared feature exactly
competing definitions are considered where material
formal definitions type-check or are clearly marked informal
a reader can distinguish every neighboring concept
Evidence Adequacy: each major evidential claim identifies its support
support is retrievable or its absence is explicit
support is relevant to the exact claim
support increases the likelihood of the claim
sample size and selection are adequate where applicable
measurement uncertainty is reported where applicable
controls or comparison conditions are present where applicable
formal receipts match the theorem actually claimed
historical claims distinguish primary and secondary testimony
philosophical premises receive arguments rather than borrowed prestige
theological claims identify their confessional or revelatory basis
independent evidence is distinguished from repeated evidence
citation quantity is not substituted for support quality
decorative equations and tables receive no evidential credit
central conclusion is proportionate to total support
Explanatory Compression: the account explains the central phenomenon
the account explains multiple facts with shared structure
unsupported bridge commitments are explicitly counted
ad hoc rescue assumptions are absent or penalized
the simpler sufficient rival is identified
added complexity explains an additional fact
the account does not merely rename the phenomenon
the mechanism is more informative than the label
compression does not erase relevant distinctions
scope of explanation is clearly bounded
predictions are generated beyond accommodated facts
the same machinery works across cited cases
failed cases are explained rather than omitted
the minimum sufficient account is stated
Rival Discrimination: rivals are stated in terms their advocates could accept
the preferred view and rivals explain the same target
a discriminating observation or theorem is proposed
the evidence is more expected under the preferred account
the evidence is not equally predicted by a rival
brute-fact rivals are assessed rather than dismissed
the preferred account faces the same standard
a possible reversal of preference is stated
the surviving comparative advantage is explicit
Testability and Falsifiability: central claims have explicit defeat conditions
predictions are stated before outcome interpretation where possible
predictions are measurable or formally decidable
thresholds or expected ranges are given where possible
failure outcomes are distinguishable from success outcomes
tests discriminate the preferred account from rivals
failed predictions cannot be rescued without recorded cost
formal claims name a proof or countermodel path
empirical claims name data and method requirements
historical claims name possible disconfirming evidence
bridge claims name mapping failure conditions
analogy claims name where the analogy breaks
replication or independent checking is possible
what would change the verdict is stated
Cross-Domain Integrity: each domain is defined independently before mapping
the mapping is stated term by term
shared relations or operations are named
translation is not treated as ontological identity
analogy is not promoted to isomorphism
isomorphism claims include a bijection or appropriate equivalence
inverse mapping is tested where claimed
negative relations and non-relations are preserved
composition or operation preservation is tested
evidence does not transfer automatically across the bridge
formal proof does not certify the semantic identification
physical results are not made theological by relabeling
theological commitments do not repair weak physics
the bridge produces new compression, prediction, or explanation
Adversarial Robustness: central premises are denied one at a time
role or label permutations are attempted
causal direction is reversed where meaningful
formalization is checked for triviality by definition
a weaker rival explanation is attempted
known objections receive their strongest form
the preferred conclusion is not protected by moving criteria
failures are preserved rather than rewritten away
a nontrivial core survives the full gauntlet
Epistemic Calibration: every claim has an appropriate epistemic mode
formal verification is distinguished from semantic truth
empirical support is distinguished from deduction
historical inference is distinguished from experiment
theological commitment is stated as such
possibility is not presented as probability
probability is not presented as certainty
local results are not presented as global results
score is not presented as truth probability
absence of evidence is not evidence of absence without argument
negative results are reported with equal visibility
public wording matches the strongest warranted conclusion
